source_note: All source texts are original, written for these fixtures about fictional places and people, and released under CC0-1.0. Two stories share a topic (coastal works) so that negatives are not trivially distinguishable by vocabulary.

vectors.notes: Oxford comma, '1 October' for 'the first of October', '£4.2m' for 'four point two million', 'about' for 'around'. Typical sub-editing.
A condensed rewrite that keeps names, figures and a few phrases. Below threshold by design; the boundary case two verifiers must agree on.
One paragraph of the reference compared at document unit. Falls well below threshold: this is why block unit exists. See version-block-excerpt.

Later version: sentence appended to paragraph 1, paragraph 4 removed, new paragraph inserted. At document unit the score moves below threshold. Expected behaviour, not a failure; the same article updated is a different document to a document-level code.
Lightly edited paragraph 2 matched against the best reference block. Block-level correlation persists where the document-level score does not.
Different story, same topic and length. Note the score sits near 0.5, which is the expected value for unrelated 64-bit codes; scores in the 0.4 to 0.6 band carry no information.
Full paraphrase preserving every fact. Listed in the scheme's known_defeats; the fixture documents that a no_match here is expected and is not evidence of non-use.
